questions.chapter_title: Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: What is the orbital description of the transition state in a classic Diels-Alder reaction between 1,3-butadiene and ethylene?

options.label: A
options.text: A carbocation-carbanion zwitterionic intermediate.

options.label: B
options.text: An electrocyclic 4-electron antiaromatic transition state.

options.label: C
options.text: A concerted, aromatic 6π electron transition state where the HOMO of the diene (ψ₂) overlaps suprafacially with the LUMO of the dienophile (π*).

options.label: D
options.text: A stepwise biradical intermediate formed by end-to-end coupling.

questions.correct_answer: A concerted, aromatic 6π electron transition state where the HOMO of the diene (ψ₂) overlaps suprafacially with the LUMO of the dienophile (π*).
questions.explanation: The thermal Diels-Alder reaction is a concerted, suprafacial [4π_s + 2π_s] cycloaddition allowed by the Woodward-Hoffmann orbital symmetry rules.

questions.chapter_title: Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: What is the mechanistic cause of the endo selectivity in the Diels-Alder reaction of cyclopentadiene with maleic anhydride?

options.label: A
options.text: The reaction proceeds via a radical anion intermediate.

options.label: B
options.text: Favorable secondary orbital overlap between the developing π system of the diene and the carbonyl π orbitals of the electron-withdrawing dienophile stabilizes the endo transition state.

options.label: C
options.text: The exo transition state experiences severe angle strain.

options.label: D
options.text: The endo product is thermodynamically more stable than the exo product.

questions.correct_answer: Favorable secondary orbital overlap between the developing π system of the diene and the carbonyl π orbitals of the electron-withdrawing dienophile stabilizes the endo transition state.
questions.explanation: Secondary orbital overlap between non-bonding portions of the diene and dienophile carbonyls lowers the activation energy for the endo pathway.

questions.chapter_title: Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: Why is (2Z,4Z)-hexadiene significantly less reactive in Diels-Alder reactions than (2E,4E)-hexadiene?

options.label: A
options.text: The (2Z,4Z) isomer has an odd number of double bonds.

options.label: B
options.text: The (2Z,4Z) isomer is an antiaromatic molecule.

options.label: C
options.text: The (2Z,4Z) isomer cannot absorb light.

options.label: D
options.text: In the required s-cis conformation, the two terminal methyl groups in the (2Z,4Z) isomer clash sterically, destabilizing the s-cis geometry needed for cycloaddition.

questions.correct_answer: In the required s-cis conformation, the two terminal methyl groups in the (2Z,4Z) isomer clash sterically, destabilizing the s-cis geometry needed for cycloaddition.
questions.explanation: Dienes must adopt the s-cis conformation to react in Diels-Alder; steric clash between internal substituents severely penalizes s-cis population.

questions.chapter_title: Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: In the addition of HBr to 1,3-butadiene, what intermediate accounts for both 1,2- and 1,4-addition products?

options.label: A
options.text: An allylic carbocation intermediate [CH₃-CH⁺-CH=CH₂ ↔ CH₃-CH=CH-CH₂⁺] where positive charge is delocalized over C2 and C4.

options.label: B
options.text: A cyclic bromonium ion intermediate.

options.label: C
options.text: A 1,4-diradical intermediate.

options.label: D
options.text: A primary carbocation intermediate.

questions.correct_answer: An allylic carbocation intermediate [CH₃-CH⁺-CH=CH₂ ↔ CH₃-CH=CH-CH₂⁺] where positive charge is delocalized over C2 and C4.
questions.explanation: Protonation at C1 generates a resonance-stabilized allylic carbocation, which can be captured by bromide at C2 (1,2) or C4 (1,4).

questions.chapter_title: Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions
questions.topic: Thermal Electrocyclic Ring Closure Conrotatory Rule
questions.question: According to the Woodward-Hoffmann rules, why does thermal ring closure of (2E,4E)-hexadiene yield cis-3,4-dimethylcyclobutene?

options.label: A
options.text: Thermal reactions always produce trans stereoisomers.

options.label: B
options.text: The reaction proceeds via a free radical mechanism.

options.label: C
options.text: The reaction proceeds through disrotatory motion to minimize steric clash.

options.label: D
options.text: Thermal electrocyclic reactions of 4n systems utilize the HOMO (ψ₂), which has opposite orbital symmetry at the termini, requiring conrotatory rotation to achieve bonding overlap.

questions.correct_answer: Thermal electrocyclic reactions of 4n systems utilize the HOMO (ψ₂), which has opposite orbital symmetry at the termini, requiring conrotatory rotation to achieve bonding overlap.
questions.explanation: The HOMO of a 4π system requires conrotatory (same-direction) orbital rotation under thermal conditions for constructive in-phase overlap.

questions.chapter_title: Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: Why does photochemical ring closure of (2E,4E)-hexadiene produce trans-3,4-dimethylcyclobutene?

options.label: A
options.text: Light heats the reaction to 1000°C.

options.label: B
options.text: Light excites an electron to the ψ₃* orbital (new HOMO), reversing terminal orbital phase symmetry and enforcing disrotatory (opposite-direction) motion for bonding overlap.

options.label: C
options.text: The reaction proceeds via an SN2 displacement.

options.label: D
options.text: Photons destroy the methyl groups.

questions.correct_answer: Light excites an electron to the ψ₃* orbital (new HOMO), reversing terminal orbital phase symmetry and enforcing disrotatory (opposite-direction) motion for bonding overlap.
questions.explanation: Photochemical excitation inverts the orbital symmetry of the HOMO, switching the allowed symmetry pathway from conrotatory to disrotatory.

questions.chapter_title: Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: What is the transition state geometry of the degenerate Cope rearrangement of 1,5-hexadiene at 300°C?

options.label: A
options.text: An ionic pathway involving an allylic carbocation.

options.label: B
options.text: A planar boat-like transition state with 8 electrons.

options.label: C
options.text: A stepwise pathway involving two allyl radicals.

options.label: D
options.text: A concerted, six-membered chair-like transition state involving the simultaneous breaking of one C-C σ bond and making of a new C-C σ bond with π bond shift.

questions.correct_answer: A concerted, six-membered chair-like transition state involving the simultaneous breaking of one C-C σ bond and making of a new C-C σ bond with π bond shift.
questions.explanation: The Cope rearrangement is a concerted [3,3]-sigmatropic shift proceeding preferentially through a chair-like six-membered transition state.

questions.chapter_title: Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions
questions.topic: Claisen Rearrangement of Allyl Phenyl Ether
questions.question: What is the sequence of mechanistic events in the thermal Claisen rearrangement of allyl phenyl ether?

options.label: A
options.text: Concerted [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement to a cyclohexadienone intermediate, followed by rapid tautomerization (enolization) to restore aromaticity, yielding ortho-allylphenol.

options.label: B
options.text: Homolytic cleavage to phenoxy radical followed by recombination.

options.label: C
options.text: Direct electrophilic attack of allyl cation onto the ring.

options.label: D
options.text: SN2 displacement of phenoxide by allyl radical.

questions.correct_answer: Concerted [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement to a cyclohexadienone intermediate, followed by rapid tautomerization (enolization) to restore aromaticity, yielding ortho-allylphenol.
questions.explanation: Thermal [3,3]-shift yields an unconjugated cyclohexadienone intermediate whose enolization is driven by the immense stabilization of restoring aromaticity.

questions.chapter_title: Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: Why does dicyclopentadiene crack into monomeric cyclopentadiene upon heating to 180°C?

options.label: A
options.text: Cyclopentadiene has higher boiling point than the dimer.

options.label: B
options.text: The dimer is an antiaromatic complex.

options.label: C
options.text: The retro-Diels-Alder reaction splits one molecule into two molecules, driven by a large positive entropy change (ΔS° > 0) that dominates at elevated temperatures (-TΔS°).

options.label: D
options.text: The monomer is stabilized by resonance with iron.

questions.correct_answer: The retro-Diels-Alder reaction splits one molecule into two molecules, driven by a large positive entropy change (ΔS° > 0) that dominates at elevated temperatures (-TΔS°).
questions.explanation: Splitting one reactant into two products increases entropy (ΔS > 0), making the retro-reaction thermodynamically favorable at high temperatures (ΔG = ΔH - TΔS).

questions.chapter_title: Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: Why does β-carotene (11 conjugated double bonds) absorb visible light (orange, 450 nm) whereas 1,3-butadiene absorbs in the far UV (217 nm)?

options.label: A
options.text: β-Carotene contains heavier carbon atoms.

options.label: B
options.text: Extended π conjugation increases the number of molecular orbitals, steadily decreasing the energy gap (ΔE) between the HOMO and LUMO into the visible spectrum.

options.label: C
options.text: 1,3-Butadiene reflects all wavelengths of light.

options.label: D
options.text: β-Carotene is a radical cation in solution.

questions.correct_answer: Extended π conjugation increases the number of molecular orbitals, steadily decreasing the energy gap (ΔE) between the HOMO and LUMO into the visible spectrum.
questions.explanation: Increasing conjugation narrows the HOMO-LUMO energy gap; smaller ΔE corresponds to absorption of longer wavelength light (E = hc/λ).

questions.question: Why does dicyclopentadiene crack into monomeric cyclopentadiene upon heating to 180°C?

options.label: B

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Thermal electrocyclic reactions of 4n systems utilize the HOMO (ψ₂), which has opposite orbital symmetry at the termini, requiring conrotatory rotation to achieve bonding overlap.

options.label: C

questions.explanation: The HOMO of a 4π system requires conrotatory (same-direction) orbital rotation under thermal conditions for constructive in-phase overlap.
